column3: 劳 is to comfort or thank. Several alternatives retain an obscure confession. The fluent option changes comforting into arrival.
田 and 甲第 are property. 甲士 changes houses into soldiers. Several compressed alternatives preserve both gifts.
高后 is the empress, not a temporal adverb. Repetition of 诸吕 obscures her relatives.
卒 is finally in this sentence. Death is the wrong predicate.
Several alternatives preserve a warning but lose the meaning of 图 or distort 千载.
The vernacular gloss conveys putting the letter away and doubt. Other choices largely leave the first clause untranslated.
The object of the arrest is a person. 以来 erroneously turns return into a temporal phrase.
Came back from Jinyang needs both the direction and the movement. 从晋阳 without a verb is incomplete.
The speaker promises to save his interlocutor. 握的手 loses whose hand, and 活公 is still opaque.
The versions with 有 reverse the claim about Former Han. The fluent option changes 庐江 to 庐汀.
Several variants modernize the killing only. The full version also renders the occupation and county office.
事齐 means to serve or assist Qi. 王的事迹 invents the king's deeds and destroys the condition.
The gloss identifies both kinds of gifts. Several answers introduce a person's name or corrupt 拜见之赀.
The surname 宋 is followed by removal from office. The expanded gloss conveys this but corrupts the minister's name.
The emperor agrees with the addressee. Several variants introduce 我 or the Yellow Emperor.
The fluent passage about a large rock is unrelated. Two partial paraphrases retain acceptance and departure.
He writes verse censuring himself. The modern gloss conveys this despite a typographical error in its closing phrase.
The recorded sentence omits the grant and adds an account of summoning. Several candidates corrupt the recipient or leave the appointment ambiguous.
